changelog:
# Changelog

## v0.5

- Raise app master volume to 200%, retaining the 70% default and independent system volume; boosted peaks are clipped to the PCM range.
- Give Don and Ka one voice each: same-sound hits replace the previous tail with a short fade. Normal Don, drumrolls, and balloons share the Don voice.
- Preserve drum-sound pitch and natural duration across playback speeds while hit timing follows the chart.
- Add saved GPIO pulse widths from 25 to 100 ms in 5 ms steps, defaulting to 70 ms, under GPIO Setting.
- Wait for input while paused instead of repeatedly recalculating and redrawing the static chart.
- Add a separate Momentum mntm-012 build for API 87.1, confirmed working by the author on Momentum CN v1.1.6; retain official and mntm-009 builds.

## v0.4

- Add a saved target display frame rate from 15 to 60 FPS in 1 FPS steps, defaulting to 50 FPS.
- Preserve audio and hit scheduling independently of the selected display frame rate.
- Replace the drum sounds with unmodified TJAPlayer3 SimpleStyle assets and retain their MIT attribution in converted resources and packages.
- Add GPL-3.0-or-later licensing, an original device screenshot, and catalog metadata.
- Split detailed documentation into user, chart-support, and development guides, and add an English README.

## v0.3

- Prevent automatic drumroll and balloon hits from accumulating sound tails; fade out the previous automatic hit before retriggering.
- Raise the automatic-hit cap to 32 hits per second.
- Smooth big-note, drumroll, drum-indicator, and balloon pixel contours.
- Improve balloon head sizing and preserve its complete hit ring.
- Reduce repeated mixer work and reuse drawing text storage.
- Improve allocation checks and cleanup when audio startup fails.

## v0.2

- Add hit-ring feedback for normal and big Don/Ka notes.
- Refine GOGO TIME effects and align the playback-time and difficulty labels.
- Release finished audio workers and buffers promptly.
- Reduce memory peaks when changing difficulty and recover the previous chart on failure.
- Add heap exhaustion, fragmentation, retry, and speed-change rollback tests.

## v0.1

- Initial release with TJA chart playback and PCM backing audio.
- Add scrolling notes, automatic drum sounds, drumrolls, balloons, and GOGO TIME.
- Add difficulty, playback-speed, scroll-speed, seeking, and volume controls.
- Add configurable GPIO drum-hit outputs and saved preferences.
description:
# Taiko Player

A lightweight TJA chart player for Flipper Zero. Play backing music through the built-in speaker, watch scrolling notes, and optionally send drum-hit pulses to external hardware.

## Features

- Normal and big Don/Ka notes, drumrolls, balloons, and GOGO TIME effects.
- Automatic drum-sound mixing with alternating left/right drum indicators; Don/Ka pitch stays fixed across playback speeds and same-sound hits replace old tails.
- Difficulty selection, pause, restart, song selection, and adjustable seeking intervals.
- Independent playback speed, scroll speed, and volume controls, including 0-200% app master volume.
- Target display refresh rate from 15 to 60 FPS, with 50 FPS as the default.
- Per-note scroll speed changes, including reverse scrolling.
- Four configurable GPIO outputs, disabled at startup.
- Saved volume, speed, frame-rate, seeking, GPIO pin and pulse-width preferences.

## Before playing

An SD card and your own TJA charts with matching audio are required. Convert audio on your computer with Python 3, FFmpeg, and the provided conversion scripts. The device plays unsigned 8-bit mono PCM WAV and does not decode OGG directly.

Catalog installation provides the app. Songs and optional drum sounds must be copied to the SD card separately. Place prepared songs under /ext/apps_data/taiko_player/songs/ and drum sounds under /ext/apps_data/taiko_player/sfx/. Without drum sounds, backing audio still plays.

Follow the [English setup instructions](https://github.com/ZeroNinx/flipper-zero-taiko-player/blob/main/README.en.md) to prepare songs and drum sounds. No additional hardware is needed for speaker playback.

## Controls

- OK: play or pause; replay after the song finishes.
- Left / Right: seek backward or forward.
- Up / Down: adjust app volume.
- Short Back: open the menu or return.
- Hold Back during playback: exit.

GPIO is optional. It uses 3.3 V logic and 70 ms high pulses by default (25–100 ms in 5 ms steps, set in GPIO Setting → Pulse Width); connect the receiver to Flipper's GND. Choose pins in GPIO Setting before enabling GPIO Output.

## Limitations

This is an automatic chart player, without hit judgment. Branching charts and Dan courses are not supported. Playback-speed changes also change pitch. Precise audio, display, and GPIO synchronization is not guaranteed.

The project is licensed under GPL-3.0-or-later. Default drum sounds are from TJAPlayer3's SimpleStyle skin under MIT; retain their attribution and license when redistributing them.
